extracted.subtask_description: AP-style newspaper coverage of World War II events, including battle reports, casualty lists, diplomatic incidents, press freedom issues, and first-person accounts of treatment of prisoners. Mixes straight reporting, dispatches, and opinion/analysis pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geneva Convention treatment of prisoners of war
rubrics_metrics.description: "Japan had agreed, in signing the Geneva Convention, to treat them as such. The captured American flyers were prisoners of war, plain and simple. They were not spies."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article asserts a legal standard: signatory states must treat captured airmen as POWs under the Geneva Convention. Surrounding text accuses Japan of breaking that obligation—subjecting prisoners to torture, forced confessions and sham trials—and argues that the executions were unlawful and cloaked with legal sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Red Cross investigation principles (memorandum of Sept. 12, 1939)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The committee cannot itself constitute a commission or name any of its members as arbiters; the committee can appoint qualified persons if all disputants agree; the committee cannot participate in an investigation or interpret findings unless specifically authorized by international convention, in advance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of procedural limits on Red Cross-related committees: they may only appoint experts by mutual consent of disputants; they may not unilaterally conduct or interpret investigations unless conventions authorize such action. The piece notes no applicable convention exists for the current claims, limiting investigatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press independence — avoid government-paid advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: "Your position that the press should not accept government paid advertising lest it be 'misconstrued as a subsidy' is sound. . . A free press absolutely unfettered, is the greatest American heritage to be preserved."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative principle urged by the American Association of Small Business: newspapers should refuse government-paid advertising to avoid appearance of subsidy and to protect press independence. The telegram also urged that the press be permitted representation at an international food conference and asked Congress to safeguard press liberties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty and role of war correspondents — witness despite danger
rubrics_metrics.description: "American war correspondents face death ('in order that we may observe in hourly action one of the freedoms for which we fight, the freedom of the press.')"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/ethical claim about reporter conduct: correspondents should risk danger to inform the public and uphold the freedom of the press. Presented as justification for frontline reporting and as a standard of professional devotion.
